correctness.rationale: At a vertex an even positive degree cannot be carried by only one odd multiplicity, so both colors of the opposite parity-side palette occur and occur oddly. Thus for either side the indicator solves Bf=1; the other indicator works because B1=0. A coordinate half of the side gives a solution (neighbor counts 1 and d-1). Independently, write the full binary adjacency matrix in last-coordinate slices as A=[[P,I],[I,P]], with P the adjacency of Q_(d-1). The coordinate flips commute in characteristic two, so P^2=I, and the kernel is the graph of P with dimension 2^(d-1). In parity order A has off-diagonal blocks B and B^T, so rank B=2^(d-2). Also A^2=0, giving BB^T=B^TB=0; rank half implies that the image of each transpose equals the kernel of its opposite block, hence each side kernel equals its orthogonal complement. Constants are ruled out as solutions, so all palettes are used. The independent side choices yield the stated sixfold named count and a free 24-fold renaming quotient. For the four-color minimum, a putative three-coloring forces (I+A)h=1 for every color indicator h; squaring I+A gives I, hence h=1 for each color, impossible. Two and one colors are excluded by even positive degree and properness, respectively. The argument includes d=2 and makes no count for nonsplit colorings.
